desc:
Given the fraction p / q, find the fraction a / b whose value is closest to it, among all fractions with a a non-negative integer and 1 ≤ b ≤ limit.

Ties are broken as follows: prefer the smaller denominator b; if the denominators are also equal, prefer the smaller numerator a. Report the answer in lowest terms as the string "a/b", so a whole number is written as "a/1".

p = 7, q = 3, limit = 2  -> "5/2"   (5/2 is 1/6 away, 2/1 is 1/3 away)
p = 9, q = 4, limit = 3  -> "7/3"
p = 1, q = 2, limit = 1  -> "0/1"   (0/1 and 1/1 tie; the smaller numerator wins)
hints: For a fixed denominator b, only the two numerators next to p * b / q can be closest. So you need at most two candidates per denominator.
Compare distances exactly. The distance of a / b from p / q is |a * q - p * b| / (b * q), and two such distances can be compared by cross-multiplying.

Go through the denominators in increasing order and replace the best candidate only on a strictly smaller distance. Try the floor numerator before the ceiling one, and reduce the final fraction by the gcd.
editorial: Any candidate a / b with a fixed b is best when a is the integer nearest to p * b / q, so only floor(p * b / q) and the next integer need checking. Over all denominators up to limit that is at most 40,000 candidates.

Distances are rational, so compare them without floating point: the distance nd / dd is smaller than best_nd / best_dd exactly when nd * best_dd < best_nd * dd. Because the denominators are scanned in increasing order and only a strictly better candidate replaces the current one, ties keep the smaller denominator. Within one denominator the smaller numerator is tried first and wins ties. Equal fractions with a larger denominator are never chosen, so the final answer is already in lowest terms, and the gcd only removes a common factor if one slipped through.
